questions.stem: Which is the correct sitting posture for keyboarding?
options: Sit upright with feet flat on the floor
Lean forward with the chin on the desk
Sit with legs crossed on the chair
Bend the back and rest the elbows on the keys
questions.explanation: Good posture prevents tiredness and errors.

questions.stem: One importance of keyboarding skill is that it
options: helps one to produce documents quickly
reduces the electricity bills of offices
questions.explanation: Good keyboarding saves time and gives neat work.

questions.stem: While keyboarding, the operator's eyes should be mainly on the
questions.explanation: Touch typists look at the copy, not the keys.

questions.stem: The computer keyboard is mainly used to
options: display pictures and videos to the user
enter text and commands into the computer
print documents on paper for filing
store files permanently in the computer
questions.explanation: The keyboard is an input device.

questions.stem: Which of these is found on a computer keyboard but NOT on a manual typewriter?
questions.explanation: Function keys exist only on computer keyboards.

questions.stem: A similarity between the typewriter keyboard and the computer keyboard is that both
options: use the QWERTY arrangement of letter keys
come with a mouse for pointing
have function keys from F1 to F12
have a screen to display the text
questions.explanation: Both use the QWERTY layout.

questions.stem: Which item is used to protect a computer from dust when not in use?
questions.explanation: A dust cover keeps dust off the computer.

questions.stem: Why should food and drinks be kept away from the computer?
options: Food makes the computer work faster
Drinks help to cool the computer down
Spills can damage the keyboard and other parts
Food and drinks improve typing speed
questions.explanation: Liquids and crumbs can damage keys and circuits.

questions.stem: A device that protects a computer from sudden changes in electricity supply is a
questions.explanation: Stabilisers and UPS units protect against power surges and failures.

questions.stem: The correct way to switch off a computer is to
options: pull out the plug while it is still working
press the reset button again and again
pour cold water on it to cool it down
shut it down properly before switching off power
questions.explanation: Proper shutdown prevents damage and data loss.

questions.topic: Correct Keyboarding Techniques and Home Row Keys
questions.stem: The home row keys for the left hand are
questions.explanation: The left fingers rest on A, S, D and F.

questions.topic: Correct Keyboarding Techniques and Home Row Keys
questions.stem: The home row keys for the right hand are
questions.explanation: The right fingers rest on J, K, L and semicolon.

questions.topic: Correct Keyboarding Techniques and Home Row Keys
questions.stem: The two keys with small bumps that help the typist find the home row without looking are
questions.explanation: The bumps on F and J guide the index fingers.

questions.topic: Correct Keyboarding Techniques and Home Row Keys
questions.stem: The space bar is struck with the
questions.explanation: The thumbs operate the space bar.

questions.topic: Correct Keyboarding Techniques and Home Row Keys
questions.stem: The row of keys containing Q, W, E, R, T and Y is the
questions.explanation: Q W E R T Y is the upper (third) row.

questions.topic: Correct Keyboarding Techniques and Home Row Keys
questions.stem: The keyboard row that contains Z, X, C, V and B is the
questions.explanation: Z X C V B are on the bottom row.

questions.topic: Correct Keyboarding Techniques and Home Row Keys
questions.stem: The letter G is struck by the
questions.explanation: G is reached by the left index finger from F.

questions.stem: Printer correction signs are also called
questions.explanation: They show the typist what corrections to make.

questions.stem: The correction sign "stet" means
questions.explanation: Stet tells the typist to keep the original text.

questions.stem: The abbreviation "uc" in a printer correction means
options: use a colon in place of a comma
questions.explanation: uc means capital letters.

questions.stem: The correction "trs" in the margin tells the typist to
options: type the marked words in red ink
trim the space between the lines
questions.explanation: trs means transpose.

questions.stem: The sign "NP" or "//" in a draft means
questions.explanation: NP means new paragraph.

questions.stem: A sentence that contains all 26 letters of the alphabet is called
questions.explanation: Alphabetic sentences help practise every key.

questions.stem: To improve keyboarding speed, a learner should
options: look at the keys all the time
questions.explanation: Regular timed drills build speed.

questions.stem: A typist keyboarded 300 words in 6 minutes. What is the speed in words per minute?
questions.explanation: Speed = 300 ÷ 6 = 50 words per minute.

questions.stem: Which practice best improves accuracy in keyboarding?
options: Typing as fast as possible, ignoring errors
Looking at the keyboard all the time
Using the backspace key after every word
questions.explanation: Accuracy comes first; speed follows with practice.

questions.stem: The Enter key on a computer keyboard is used to
options: delete the character to the left
move the cursor to a new line
questions.explanation: Pressing Enter starts a new line.

questions.stem: On a typewriter, the line space regulator is used to
options: change the colour of the ink
remove the paper from the machine
lock the keys in capital letters
questions.explanation: It sets single, double or other line spacing.

questions.stem: In a word processor, a table is inserted using the
questions.explanation: The Insert/Create Table command creates rows and columns.

questions.stem: The part of a business letter that shows the sender's address is the
questions.explanation: The heading carries the sender's address and date.

questions.stem: "Dear Sir" in a business letter is called the
questions.explanation: The salutation greets the reader.

questions.stem: The main message of a business letter is written in the
questions.explanation: The body contains the message.

questions.stem: "Yours faithfully" is used as the complimentary close when the salutation is
questions.explanation: "Dear Sir/Madam" goes with "Yours faithfully".

questions.stem: The letter style in which every line begins at the left margin is the
questions.explanation: In fully blocked style all lines start at the margin.

questions.stem: Alphanumeric keys are keys that contain
questions.explanation: Alpha means letters; numeric means numbers.

questions.stem: The keys should be struck with
questions.explanation: A light touch prevents errors and fatigue.

questions.stem: The figures 1 to 0 on the main keyboard are found on the
questions.explanation: The number keys are on the top row.

questions.stem: The key used to type a single capital letter is the
questions.explanation: Hold Shift while pressing a letter for a capital.

questions.stem: The key that makes all letters capital until pressed again is
questions.explanation: Caps Lock locks the keyboard in capitals.

questions.stem: The key that deletes the character to the left of the cursor is
questions.explanation: Backspace removes the character before the cursor.

questions.stem: The key used to move the cursor to preset points, for example when indenting a paragraph, is the
questions.explanation: Tab jumps to the next tab stop.

questions.stem: In typing, how many spaces are traditionally left after a comma?
questions.explanation: One space follows a comma.

questions.stem: No space is left
options: after a comma in a list
questions.explanation: Punctuation marks are typed close to the word before them.

questions.stem: Which sentence is correctly spaced?
options: We sell pens, books and bags.
We sell pens , books and bags.
questions.explanation: A comma is attached to the word before it and followed by one space.

questions.stem: A paragraph in which all lines start at the left margin is a
questions.explanation: Blocked paragraphs start every line at the margin.

questions.stem: A paragraph in which only the first line starts a few spaces in from the margin is
questions.explanation: Only the first line is indented.

questions.stem: A paragraph whose first line starts at the margin while the other lines are set in is
questions.explanation: The first line "hangs" out to the left.

questions.stem: In a word processor, the Page Setup dialogue is used to change the
options: spelling of words in the text
questions.explanation: Page Setup controls the layout of the page.

questions.stem: A page set so that it is wider than it is tall is in
questions.explanation: Landscape is wider than tall.

questions.stem: Text arranged so that both the left and right edges are straight is said to be
questions.explanation: Justified text is aligned on both margins.

questions.stem: A memorandum (memo) is used mainly for communication
questions.explanation: Memos are internal messages.

questions.stem: Which of these headings is found in a memo?
questions.explanation: A memo has From, To, Date and Subject headings.

questions.stem: In an e-mail, the "Subject" line tells the receiver
options: the time zone of the sender
questions.explanation: The subject line summarises the message.

questions.stem: In an e-mail, the "Cc" field is used to
options: delete the message after reading it
change the font of the message
send a copy of the message to someone else
attach a printer to the computer
questions.explanation: Cc means carbon copy.

questions.stem: Which of these is a feature of e-mail?
options: It must be posted in an envelope
It needs a postage stamp to be sent
Messages can be delivered almost instantly
questions.explanation: E-mail is fast and can carry attachments.

questions.stem: Tabulation means
options: writing a long essay on a topic
arranging information in columns and rows
sending an e-mail to a customer
questions.explanation: Tables present data in rows and columns.

questions.stem: In a table, the horizontal lines of cells are called
questions.explanation: Rows run across; columns run down.

questions.stem: A typist is to create a table to list 12 students and their scores in 3 subjects, with one row for headings. How many rows are needed?
questions.explanation: 12 student rows plus 1 heading row = 13 rows.
